title: Pakistan FBR Annex-F — Personal Expenses
description: The Federal Board of Revenue's (FBR) official 'Manual Return' workbook for individuals, Tax Year 2024 edition, worksheet 'Annex-F' — the schedule of a taxpayer's personal and household expenses for the tax year (rent, rates/taxes/charge/cess, vehicle running/maintenance, travelling, utilities, insurance/security, medical, educational, club, functions/gatherings, donations/Zakat/annuity/profit-on-debt/life-insurance-premium, and other personal/household expenses, across sixteen named categories), reconciled to a headline total (Sr. 1) that nets out contributions other family members made toward those same expenses (Sr. 17), itemised across up to four named family members in an embedded sub-table (Sr. 18 through Sr. 21, each with its own CNIC, Name, and Amount). This is the ninth and final schema authored from this same nine-worksheet workbook, alongside the already-modelled 'IND (PROP-CG-OS)' (Form IT-1B, `pk/fbr/annual-individual-income-tax-return-it-1b`), 'IND (BUS PLUS)' (Form IT-2, `pk/fbr/annual-individual-income-tax-return-it-2`), 'Annex-A' (`pk/fbr/annexure-a-adjustable-tax`), 'Annex-B' (`pk/fbr/annexure-b-manufacturing-trading-profit-loss-account`), 'Annex-C' (`pk/fbr/annexure-c-inadmissible-admissible-deductions`), 'Annex-D' (`pk/fbr/annexure-d-depreciation-amortization`), 'Annex-E' (`pk/fbr/annexure-e-minimum-final-tax-chargeable`), and 'Wealth Statement' (`pk/fbr/wealth-statement`) worksheets. Like Annex-A's and Annex-E's own Name/CNIC cells, and unlike Annex-B/Annex-C/Annex-D's own Name/CNIC cells, this worksheet's own Name and CNIC cells are plain blank entry cells, not formula-linked to the 'IND (BUS PLUS)' worksheet. This worksheet's own single `dataValidation` rule (`sqref="F6:F22 F24:F27"`) covers every Amount cell on this sheet, including both of this sheet's own headline totals (Sr. 1 and Sr. 17) alongside their own components — the same total-validated-like-its-components inversion already disclosed for Annex-A's and Annex-C's own headline totals, and the opposite of Annex-E's own headline-total exclusion. This document opens no new vertical for Pakistan (Taxes was already opened by `pk/fbr/annual-individual-income-tax-return-it-1b`); it is this workbook's ninth companion schema and the eleventh schema for Pakistan overall, and closes this workbook's own disclosed backlog (Annexes A through F, both annual return worksheets, and the Wealth Statement are now all authored). This document describes the form only; it does not submit anything on the filer's behalf, and does not imply endorsement by the Islamic Republic of Pakistan or the Federal Board of Revenue. GovSchema is independent and is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or operated by the Government of Pakistan.

verification.notes:
GOV-5782 ("GovSchema Standard Research"). Re-scanned CATALOG.md fresh first: the immediately preceding GOV-5773 cycle's own VERIFICATION.md, and this document's own workbook siblings (IT-1B, IT-2, Annex-A, Annex-B, Annex-C, Annex-D, Annex-E, Wealth Statement), had all explicitly named "Annex-F" as this workbook's sole remaining disclosed, open backlog item, after the 16-jurisdiction "5 of 6 verticals" gap list had already been re-screened a dead end across seven consecutive prior cycles (GOV-5731, GOV-5738, GOV-5745, GOV-5752, GOV-5759, GOV-5766, GOV-5773). This cycle picked up Annex-F to close this workbook's own backlog outright, rather than re-screening that same jurisdiction list an eighth consecutive time. Independently re-fetched the same workbook this cycle via plain `curl`: HTTP 200, size 104,097 bytes, sha256 `4e2f9874e9a910713fae9a182fc5c5a578bcfd2649d2031f8144c8b5fba96b9f` — byte-identical to every prior cycle's own recorded figures for this same workbook (GOV-3104, GOV-5731, GOV-5738, GOV-5745, GOV-5752, GOV-5759, GOV-5766, GOV-5773), confirming no revision. Unzipped directly via Python's `zipfile` (no `unzip`/pip/openpyxl in this environment) and confirmed via `xl/workbook.xml`'s own `<sheets>` element that `Annex-F` (`sheetId="17"`) maps to `r:id="rId8"`, which `xl/_rels/workbook.xml.rels` resolves to `xl/worksheets/sheet8.xml`; parsed that sheet's own `sheetData` rows directly via Python's `xml.etree.ElementTree`, `xl/sharedStrings.xml` table, `mergeCells`, and `dataValidations` block from the raw XML. This sheet's own `_xlnm.Print_Area` ('Annex-F'!$A$1:$F$28, from `xl/workbook.xml`'s own `definedNames`) was cross-checked against the sheet's own populated content (rows 1–28, plus scattered decorative cells in columns G through P outside the print area, none carrying any label or value, disregarded) and found to match.

This worksheet's own header block (rows 3-4) matches Annex-A's and Annex-E's own plain-header convention, not Annex-B/Annex-C/Annex-D's own formula-linked convention: Name (cell C3, merged C3:D3) and CNIC (cell C4, merged C4:D4) are both plain blank cells with no `<f>` formula element — confirmed by direct inspection of the raw cell XML. Tax Year (cell F3) is pre-filled "2024". NTN (cell F4) is a genuine direct-entry cell but, unlike Annex-B's/Annex-C's/Annex-D's/Annex-E's own NTN cells, is not covered by this sheet's own single `dataValidation` rule (`sqref="F6:F22 F24:F27"`) — the same uncovered shape already disclosed for Annex-A's own NTN cell.

This worksheet's own single `dataValidation` rule (`type="whole"`, `operator="greaterThanOrEqual"`, `formula1=0`, `sqref="F6:F22 F24:F27"`) was independently parsed: it covers every Amount cell in both the sixteen-category personal-expense table (rows 6–22, Sr. 1 through Sr. 17) and the four-row family-contribution sub-table (rows 24–27, Sr. 18 through Sr. 21) — including both of this sheet's own headline totals (Sr. 1, row 6; Sr. 17, row 22) alongside their own components, the same total-validated-like-its-components pattern already disclosed for Annex-A's and Annex-C's own headline totals, and the opposite of Annex-E's own headline-total exclusion. Every printed, fillable cell is nonetheless modelled as a field regardless of validation coverage, consistent with this workbook's own established convention.

The family-contribution sub-table (rows 23–27) has its own two-column header at row 23 ("CNIC No.", cell C23; "Name*", cell D23) with no repeated "Amount" header of its own — the sub-table's own Amount column (F) is understood to inherit the main table's own row-5 "Amount" header, confirmed by this column's own continuous `dataValidation` coverage (`F24:F27`) and consistent cell styling across both tables. Column E carries no header, no value, and no `dataValidation` coverage anywhere in this sub-table (rows 23–27) — a genuine unlabelled, non-fillable spacer column between the Name and Amount columns, disclosed and not modelled as a field.

`mergeCells` block (16 entries) independently parsed and confirmed: `A1:F1` (title), `A2:F2` (subtitle "Personal Expenses"), `A3:B3`/`C3:D3` and `A4:B4`/`C4:D4` (Name/CNIC label-and-value pairs), `C5:D5` (header "Description"), `C6:D6` through `C22:D22` (each category row's own Description cell), and `A6:A27` — the rotated "Personal Expenses" section label. Unlike Annex-E's own rotated label (`A5:A39`, falling sixteen rows short of that sheet's own last data row), this sheet's own rotated label (`A6:A27`) exactly spans this sheet's entire single-table block, including its own embedded family-contribution sub-table — the converse of Annex-E's own disclosed asymmetry, confirmed and disclosed here for completeness.

Structural findings disclosed, not corrected: (1) Sr. 4's own printed label, "Vehicle Running / Maintenence", carries a source-document spelling artifact ("Maintenence" for "Maintenance"), quoted verbatim in that field's own description and corrected in the field's own label for legibility. (2) Sr. 1's own printed formula label, "Personal Expenses [(2 + 16) - 17]", nets Sr. 17 (family contribution) back out after implicitly including it — the taxpayer's own personal expenses (Sr. 2 through Sr. 16) plus the family-member contribution total (Sr. 17), minus that same Sr. 17 again — a genuine printed-formula quirk, quoted verbatim and disclosed, not corrected or simplified. (3) The family-contribution sub-table provides exactly four bounded slots (Sr. 18 through Sr. 21) with no visible mechanism on this sheet for a fifth family member, consistent with this workbook's own established bounded-slot convention (e.g. Annex-D's own three "Intangible" slots) — modelled as four explicitly numbered field triples (`familyMemberContribution1`–`4`), not an open-ended array.
